subject: VPC egress latency attribution and carveout request — Arborly
messages:
From: Sam Rice <sam.rice@arborly.io>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Megan Torres <megan.torres@arborly.io>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: carveout for VPC egress latency attribution

Hi David,

Thanks for the hosted demo last week — Arborly is excited to move forward with Redwood Private in our AWS VPC. Before we begin the onboarding and procurement paperwork, our network/security team wants to confirm how uptime/latency SLAs will be attributed when traffic egresses our VPC to third-party CDNs and partner endpoints.

Key ask: we need an explicit carveout that excludes customer-controlled egress (including our transit/peering links and partner CDN handoff) from Redwood's latency SLA for Private deployments. Our concern is that our egress link to EdgePartner (we control the peering and routing) can introduce tail latency that is outside Redwood's control, and we want that reflected in contract language.

I'm attaching a simplified network diagram that shows the handoff points. Can you confirm what evidence Redwood would require to attribute incidents to our egress (traceroutes, flow logs, packet captures, timestamps, etc.), and whether Redwood would accept a clause that routes responsibility for egress latency to the customer in those scenarios?

Attachments: arborly_network-diagram.png (image/png)

Appreciate a quick note on next steps — we may need legal to review proposed wording before PO.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Rice
Head of Infrastructure
Arborly, Inc.
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sam Rice <sam.rice@arborly.io>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for VPC egress latency attribution

Hi Sam — thanks for the diagram and the clear ask.

High-level answer: we can discuss a narrowly scoped attribution carveout for customer-controlled egress. Redwood's standard Private SLA assumes the customer controls their VPC network and peering; however, we typically require an operational evidence protocol so that credits are only issued for incidents where Redwood infrastructure is demonstrably at fault.

As a next step I attached a draft SLA addendum that proposes (1) precise carveout language, (2) an evidence checklist (what we would need to accept an egress-attributed event), and (3) an assisted-troubleshooting runbook. Please review and flag any language you can't accept. If you prefer, we can schedule a short call with our network reliability engineer (Karthik) and our security compliance lead (Soojin).

Attachments: proposed-sla-addendum-draft.pdf (application/pdf)

Would you be available for a 30 minute call Wednesday?

—David
David Kim
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Rice <sam.rice@arborly.io>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Megan Torres <megan.torres@arborly.io>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for VPC egress latency attribution

David — thanks, received. Megan and I skimmed the draft and added inline comments in our copy. A few concrete points from Arborly:

- We are happy to provide traceroutes, VPC flow logs, and sFlow samples within 24 hours of an incident.
- Our ask is that the SLA explicitly excludes "egress tail latency caused by customer-controlled transit/peering or partner CDN handoff between the customer's VPC edge and any third-party CDN or partner network".
- We also want the addendum to include a maximum 48-hour turnaround for Redwood to accept/reject customer-submitted evidence before credits are calculated; otherwise the incident stays attributed to the customer's network.

Proposed minimal contract language (informal):
"For Private deployments where traffic egresses the customer's VPC into customer-controlled transit or peering links, Redwood's latency SLA shall not apply to delays originating on or beyond the customer's egress interface. Attribution requires: time-synchronized traceroute evidence, VPC flow logs covering the incident window, and an agreed packet-capture or sFlow sample demonstrating transit divergence."

If Redwood can commit to the 48-hour review window and the evidence checklist, we'll present to legal. We can join the call Wednesday; what time did you have in mind?

—Sam
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: (internal) Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for VPC egress latency attribution (internal suggested redline)

David/Karthik — quick internal note with suggested operational guardrails before we send final language to Arborly:

1) Evidence checklist: require NTP-synced traceroutes from both sides (customer and our probe), VPC flow logs with 1s granularity where available, and either a 30s packet capture or sFlow export showing the observed tail latency.
2) Timing: accept customer evidence submissions within 72 hours for initial triage, but guarantee Redwood will issue an acceptance/rejection decision on attribution within 48 hours of a complete evidence package. If evidence is incomplete, Redwood will request supplements and the 48-hour clock pauses.
3) Operational runbook: include a clause that Redwood may request (up to twice per quarter) remote-assisted troubleshooting sessions and that Redwood's assisted checks do not imply fault.
4) Escrow of credits: if incident is ultimately attributed to Redwood infra, credit calculation basis should be limited to the affected capacity pool rather than invoice-level credits to avoid over-crediting in shared Dedicated pools.

I'm attaching an evidence-checklist spreadsheet we can use to speed reviews. I lean toward accepting the carveout if we retain clear requirements on evidence and timelines.

Attachments: evidence-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

—Soojin
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sam Rice <sam.rice@arborly.io>, Megan Torres <megan.torres@arborly.io>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for VPC egress latency attribution

Sam/Megan — thanks for the clear proposed language and for offering the evidence up front. We reviewed internally (see Soojin's note) and have produced a redline that balances your ask with Redwood's need for an evidentiary standard and a bounded review timeline.

Summary of what Redwood can agree to now:
- Carveout: Redwood will exclude customer-controlled egress (as defined in the addendum) from Redwood's latency SLA, provided the customer supplies the evidence package described below.
- Evidence package: time-synchronized traceroutes, VPC flow logs, and a packet-capture or sFlow export that demonstrates the latency path. The evidence package must be submitted within 72 hours of the incident for initial intake; a complete package allows Redwood 48 hours to accept/reject attribution. If Redwood requests supplements because the package is incomplete, the 48-hour review period pauses.
- Assisted troubleshooting: Redwood will make an engineer available for assisted troubleshooting; performing checks does not change attribution unless agreed in writing.
- Credits: If an incident is ultimately attributed to Redwood infrastructure, credit calculations will be scoped to the affected deployment capacity pool.

I've attached a redlined addendum (redlined-sla-addendum.pdf) with the concrete language and a DocuSign link for the addendum so your legal team can review and sign if acceptable: https://docusign.net/ARB-2026-117

If that looks acceptable, Megan/Sam, approve and we can route to procurement. If you'd like a call to walk through the evidence requirements, Karthik is available tomorrow morning for a 30-minute troubleshooting/process sync.

—David
David Kim
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redlined-sla-addendum.pdf (application/pdf)
